problem: Seven persistent retrieval misses have gold documents in the corpus, and frozen generated queries place gold within BM25 top-1000 on six cases, but no case reaches any single-query top-20. Passage, dense, visible-pivot oracle transfer, and rarity-first pivot selection did not meet their gates. The project has not yet tested whether deterministic aggregation of the existing query rankings is a sufficient lower bound.
simplest_baseline: Apply uniform Reciprocal Rank Fusion with k=60 to the complete frozen generated-query BM25 top-1000 lists for each case. Do not generate a query, inspect gold during fusion, call an LLM, add a reranker, or add an Agent.
hypothesis: Cross-query rank agreement will move a gold document into the fused top-20 for at least four of seven persistent misses. If top-20 fails but fused top-100 reaches four cases, only then may a separately registered typed reranker be considered.
changed_mechanisms: uniform reciprocal-rank fusion across frozen generated-query rankings
anti_claim: This is deterministic frozen-query harness retrieval aggregation on outcome-selected development failures, not training and not a model-capability improvement.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: Before paying for parallel research contexts, fuse the retrieval lists already produced by the single frozen trajectory and measure whether candidate visibility is the actual bottleneck.
RRF is a cheaper tool-layer aggregation baseline than another reflection or compression call and preserves a direct causal link from each query rank to the fused slate.

The existing run already paid for multiple research questions. Fusing their candidates tests whether more crawling is necessary before increasing search breadth or adding a publisher-stage intervention.
RRF is the non-agent aggregation lower bound for multiple search branches; a search graph is unjustified if its fixed branch outputs cannot produce a viable shared candidate slate.

frozen_controls: same seven outcome-selected persistent retrieval misses
same trial-1 order and exact SHA256 of 48 successful generated queries
same 100,195-document full-document BM25 index and byte digests
Pyserini 1.2.0 default English analyzer with BM25 k1 0.9 and b 0.4
uniform Reciprocal Rank Fusion with k=60
deterministic tie break by best rank, occurrence count, and docid
evaluation only at fused depths 20 and 100
zero provider, online search, Judge, and GPU use
next_action: Freeze uniform RRF on this failure cluster. It recovered 0/7 at fused top-20 and 0/7 at fused top-100, versus the fixed single-query baselines of 0/7 and 2/7. Do not tune k or tie breaks on these cases and do not admit a reranker over a top-100 slate containing no gold documents. Before building an expensive passage-dense index or typed entity linker, separately register a zero-provider dense-head visibility audit that tests whether the pinned 512-token document representation can even contain the literal answer spans in the 18 gold documents.
claim_boundary: This calibration can establish only whether fixed-query rank fusion exposes gold candidates on saved failures. A later unseen paired run must lock model, retriever, query count, Token, cost, and Agent count before any effectiveness claim.
